batchName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476) - Easy Batch 2
chapterName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476)

questions.question: Which tireless general held the Western Empire together for about two decades before Attila's invasion?
questions.explanation: Aetius held the West together, fighting Goths, Franks and rebels. He often used Hunnic mercenaries to do it.
questions.sourceQuote: For two decades the West was held together by Aetius, the tireless general who fought Goths, Franks and rebels, often with Hunnic mercenaries.

questions.question: After the Roman world was split in 395, from which city was the eastern half governed?
questions.explanation: The East was ruled from Constantinople, the great city on the Bosphorus. The West, including Italy, Spain and Gaul, went to the other young son.
questions.sourceQuote: One took the East, governed from Constantinople (*Constantinopolis*), the great city on the Bosphorus.

questions.question: How long did the Vandals plunder Rome in 455?
questions.explanation: The Vandals plundered Rome for two weeks, far more thoroughly than the Goths had in 410. They sailed away with huge treasure and an imperial princess.
questions.sourceQuote: The Vandals then plundered Rome for two weeks, far more thoroughly than the Goths in 410, and sailed away with huge treasure and an imperial princess.

questions.question: When Roman envoys asked what he would leave the citizens, what did Alaric reportedly reply?
questions.explanation: Alaric reportedly answered 'Their lives.' He also laughed at the Senate's boasts, saying thick grass is easier to cut than thin.
questions.sourceQuote: Asked what he would leave the citizens, he replied: “Their lives.”

questions.question: In the early 400s, the frightened western court moved its capital from Milan to which town?
questions.explanation: The court fled to Ravenna after Alaric invaded Italy. The town was shielded by marshes and had an escape route by sea.
questions.sourceQuote: Even so, the frightened court moved its capital from Milan to Ravenna, a town near the Adriatic coast shielded by marshes and with an escape route by sea.

questions.question: In 418, where did Rome give the Visigoths land to farm?
questions.explanation: Rome settled the Visigoths in Aquitaine, in south-western France: a whole people living inside the empire under its own king.
questions.sourceQuote: In 418 Rome gave them land to farm in Aquitaine, in south-western France.

questions.question: What vast book did a North African bishop write as the most lasting answer to the sack of Rome?
questions.explanation: The bishop wrote The City of God. It argued that Christians' true home was a heavenly city, and it became one of the foundations of Christian thought.
questions.sourceQuote: The most lasting answer came from Augustine, a bishop in North Africa, who wrote a vast book called The City of God.

questions.question: Where did Aetius's coalition clash with Attila's army in 451?
questions.explanation: The armies met on the Catalaunian Plains near Troyes, in north-eastern France. They fought over a ridge until dark.
questions.sourceQuote: Around 20 June 451 the armies clashed on the Catalaunian Plains near Troyes, in north-eastern France, fighting over a ridge until dark.

questions.question: After the sack of 410, what did pagans claim had caused the disaster?
options: The Senate had grown corrupt and lazy
Rome had abandoned the ancient sacrifices
Barbarians had been let into the army
The emperor had left Rome for Ravenna
questions.explanation: Pagans said Rome had lost divine protection by giving up the old sacrifices. Christians and pagans both used the sack as ammunition.
questions.sourceQuote: Pagans argued that Rome had lost divine protection by abandoning the ancient sacrifices.

questions.question: What made the Gothic leader Alaric revolt in 395?
options: The Huns had seized his lands
He was denied a high Roman command
He was refused a Roman bride
His father was executed by Romans
questions.explanation: Alaric revolted because he was denied high Roman command. He then went on to plunder Greece.
questions.sourceQuote: Angry at being denied high Roman command, he revolted in 395 and plundered Greece.
